title: Lessons, podium finishes, and what comes next for Pepe Martí
excerpt:
Pepe Martí’s debut campaign in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship established the 21-year-old CUPRA KIRO driver as 'one to watch' in the paddock!

Pepe Martí had a rookie season he could scarcely have imagined when he joined Formula E paddock at the start of the 2025/26 season. Not only did the CUPRA KIRO driver achieve two podium finishes and end the year as the highest placed rookie, but he also made history as the first Spaniard in the championship to secure a podium.

The CUPRA KIRO driver took home 66 championship points, enough to beat fellow rookie Felipe Drugovich by just one point. However, Marti narrowly missed out on a place inside the top-10, with Round 16 (the first of the London double-header finale weekend) resulting in disappointment and a point less finish. Tokyo was also a weekend of mixed emotions, with a DNF in the second race of the weekend - the day after his teammate Dan Ticktum snatched a dramatic victory from Andretti’s Jake Dennis.

“The race (Round 16 in London) ended up with a DNF, which is what you never want," said Martí. "We got quite unlucky with the Full Course Yellow. It was thrown out for about one lap so about seven cars got a really good advantage. We weren't in that group, unfortunately. We had a good pace. I was moving forward. I would have probably finished right in front of Oliver (Rowland) in P10, so we could have scraped a point, but we weren't able to. I was not happy with myself.”

“Ideally we want to finish on a good result and on the high notes as well. Most of the team is English, it's a home race for most of them. So it would’ve also been nice for them to be able to score a good result. If I'm honest today, the main limiting factor was qualifying.”

Marti responded in the following round - the final race of the 2025/26 championship campaign - taking eighth after starting from 13th on the grid (he was classified 11th in qualifying but started 13th due to a grid penalty).

Marti maintained 13th for most of the title-deciding race before completing his two ATTACK MODE activations on Lap 23 and 31. He then battled his way into the top-10 over the final four laps to take home eighth, making it a total of 128 points for CUPRA KIRO, securing the squad its most successful campaign in Formula E to date.

“I wasn’t really happy, but I guess that goes for everyone, right? Everyone apart from the winner isn't happy,” he continued. “It's not the greatest weekend of my life, but at least we got something out of it. I managed to help with people who I needed to help during the race and also finish my own race in a good position and obviously take away some points which I'm quite grateful for in this situation than I was in five races ago.

NEWS: Pepe Martí continues with CUPRA KIRO for 2026/27 season

“I have no regrets. Obviously, there are a lot of things that I would like to improve this season and I wouldn't really call it a regret. It's stuff that I want to get better at, stuff that I need to improve and obviously stuff that as a team we need to understand and move forward.”

Marti’s racecraft and determined approach to recovering from setbacks were the highlights of his debut campaign, as he managed to score nine points finishes from 17 races and proved many critics wrong. Now, however, the 21-year-old driver is ready to leave his rookie season behind and turn his attention to a new chapter for the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship - GEN4.

“We need to regroup, and come back a bit stronger next year," he asserts. “I need some time off as a whole, since 2025 even in Formula 2, I haven't had some time off and I need to sort of really, really disconnect from the motorsport world. I just want to be alone with my family, have some time off, enjoy the time with friends, the good weather, the good food, and a lot of cycling, get back in shape. In the championship, it's very hard to maintain proper shape so we can try to get better in the winter and come back stronger in December.”

Pepe Martí will continue with CUPRA KIRO for the 2025/27 Formula E season.

title: Pepe Martí continues with CUPRA KIRO for 2026/27 season
excerpt:
After a podium winning rookie season, Pepe Martí is set to continue with the CUPRA KIRO squad into Formula E's all-new GEN4 era.

Martí, who hails from Spain and is managed by A14, the driver development group co-founded by former Formula 1 World Champion Fernando Alonso, impressed many in the paddock with his on track performances in the 2025/26 season.

After scoring points in only his second E-Prix appearance, and leading his home race in Madrid, he achieved his maiden Formula E podium in Monaco - putting on a brilliant performance, after starting from 15th. Not only was the podium a significant milestone for Martí, but it also marked the first time a Spanish driver had reached the rostrum in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

READ MORE: Pepe Martí makes his mark in Monaco

A further podium (a second place) followed at the 2026 Sanya E-Prix, with the additional points helping the CUPRA KIRO driver to finish the season as the highest-placed rookie in the Drivers’ Championship with 66 points.

Continuing with CUPRA KIRO, Martí will play a crucial role in the team’s next chapter as Formula E enters the GEN4 era, the most exciting chapter to date in the all-electric championship.

Capable of reaching speeds in excess of 335kph, 0-100kph in approximately 1.8 seconds, and 0-200kph in just 4.4 seconds - 1.5 seconds faster than its predecessor - GEN4 will deliver 50% more power in race mode than the current GEN3 Evo race car. The GEN4 car will be an average of 10 seconds faster per lap than the GEN3 car in qualifying mode. In ATTACK MODE, GEN4 produces up to 600kW of power, a 71% increase in base output over GEN3 Evo, delivering performance that pushes the limits of electric racing. GEN4 is the only single-seater race car with permanent all-wheel drive.

Unleashing GEN4: A new era of high-performance, sustainable electric racing begins

Pepe Martí, CUPRA KIRO Driver, said: “I’m very excited to continue with CUPRA KIRO for the 2026/27 Formula E season. I’ve felt a huge amount of support and trust since joining the team, and together, I think we’ve built something really positive during my rookie year. Formula E has been an incredible learning experience, and I feel that I’ve grown a lot as a driver over the course of the season. To have achieved top three finishes, led races, and become the first Spanish driver to stand on the Formula E podium is something I’m very proud of, but I also feel like we’re only just getting started. CUPRA KIRO has big ambitions for the future, and I’m excited to be part of the journey for GEN4. I can’t wait to see what we can achieve next season.”

Russell O’Hagan, CUPRA KIRO Team Principal, said: “Continuing our relationship with Pepe for the 2026/27 season was a very straightforward decision. Since the moment he joined the team, he has consistently impressed us with his talent, work ethic, and maturity. As a championship, Formula E can be particularly demanding for rookie drivers, especially at the end of a generation cycle, so our priority was always to allow Pepe the time and environment to develop without unnecessary pressure.

"The reality is, however, that he exceeded our expectations almost immediately and showed consistent performance across season. Watching Pepe grow over the course of the season was incredibly rewarding. He’s developed his understanding of Formula E’s nuances at an impressive rate, grown in confidence with every race, and delivered performances that have demonstrated exactly why we believed in him in the first place. We firmly believe he’s one of the sport’s brightest young talents and ambassadors, and that he has all the attributes to become a major force in Formula E. We’re incredibly proud of everything that Pepe has achieved during his rookie season, and the team’s role in getting him up to speed – it was a big group effort. We’re equally excited that he’ll continue his journey with CUPRA KIRO as we enter GEN4. We’re only at the beginning of what we believe we can achieve together.”

title: Zane Maloney joins Oliver Rowland at Nissan for 2026/27
excerpt:
Nissan have announced Zane Maloney will join the team alongside Oliver Rowland for the 2026/27 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

Rowland continues into a fourth year, having built a strong relationship with the Japanese manufacturer over the years, having originally joined its Formula E program as a rookie in Season 5 (2018/19) - Nissan's first year in the sport.

Since returning to the team during the GEN3 era in Season 10 (2023/24), Rowland has enjoyed some of the most successful years of his career, including claiming the Drivers' title in Season 11. In the last campaign, he earned six podiums, including a victory on the streets of Monaco, securing fourth in the Drivers' World Championship and maintaining his record of top-four finishes in every season since his return.

"I'm delighted to continue with Nissan for our seventh season together and fourth consecutive one with Nissan," says the 34-year-old. "With the GEN4 car coming in, we're going to see a big step in performance and it's something we're really excited for.

"I'm looking forward to Zane joining the team, he's had a great junior career and two years of experience in Formula E, which puts him in a good position to start Season 13 strongly. Heading into the future with Nissan Formula E Team is very exciting and we're aiming to improve on our performances from this year."

Maloney joins Nissan

Meanwhile, Maloney enters his third season in Formula E, having gained valuable experience across his first two campaigns, scoring top-10 finishes in São Paulo, Monaco and Tokyo in 2025/26.

The Barbadian earned his opportunity in Formula E after a highly successful junior career, impressing across the 2023 and 2024 Formula 2 seasons with 11 podiums, including two wins, and finishing fourth in the last year. His Formula E experience, combined with his proven pace in Formula 2, will provide a strong foundation as he enters the GEN4 era with Nissan.

"I'm very excited to join Nissan," says the 22-year-old. "When I came into Formula E, the team was winning the championship with Oli, so it's a great chance for me to now join a top manufacturer.

"I've spent the last two seasons with a new team, developing my skills and trying to get the best results we could, so I'm really looking forward to taking this next step in my career.

"It's also a great opportunity to be teammates with Oli. He's a World Champion and someone I watched when I was growing up, first winning races in Formula 2 and then in Formula E, so to be alongside him and learn from him will be really valuable.

"GEN4 is a big opportunity for everyone to develop quickly, and I'll be doing everything I can to prepare well and hit the ground running from the first race. A big thank you to Nissan for the trust in me. I'm really looking forward to getting started and achieving some very good results together."

title: Opel finalises 2026/27 line-up with Mitch Evans signing
excerpt:
Opel GSE has confirmed the capture of one of the most successful drivers in ABB FIA Formula E World Championship history with Mitch Evans joining the squad from the 2026/27 season.

The 32-year-old New Zealander has achieved the most victories in the racing series - 16 - and brings his experience from 10 years in the series to the new German manufacturer team.

Together with rookie Théo Pourchaire, Evans forms what Opel GSE view as a driver mix of top driver and young talent, underpinning the team's ambitions to compete at the front field from the start.

Dream team: Mitch Evans 'the preferred candidate from the beginning'

“We have secured our dream team. Mitch Evans was the preferred candidate for our Opel GSE Formula E Team from the very beginning. His commitment once again underlines the seriousness of the entire project,” said Opel Motorsport Director and Team Principal Jörg Schrott.

“We have already met Mitch on and off the racetrack. In addition to his undisputed exceptional sporting pedigree, he also fits perfectly into our team as a person. After so many years with another manufacturer, he was deliberately looking for a new challenge.

"Now the Opel family and Mitch are taking this next step together. In doing so, we are sending a clear message: We are joining the World Championship to challenge at the front.”

Evans: 'Perfect moment for a fresh challenge'

Evans himself is looking forward to the change and the cooperation with Opel. “I am proud to be an Opel works driver and to be part of this new chapter in Formula E. It’s great that we can finally make this step official,” said Evans.

“After ten years with a manufacturer, it was time for me to take on a fresh challenge. The leap to the GEN4 cars represents the perfect moment to start something new. I immediately felt how much energy and passion Opel is putting into the Formula E project.

"The team isn’t just coming into the series to compete: Opel is here to win, and that’s exactly what I aspire to.”

After a dramatic final weekend in London, Evans was narrowly denied the first Drivers' World Championship title of his career, but once again underlined his position among Formula E's best.

“The title clearly remains the big goal for me, in this respect I still have a score to settle in Formula E. That’s exactly why the move to Opel feels like the right new challenge for me.

"Starting a new Formula E generation with a new team and being successful right away is anything but a matter of course, but that’s exactly what appeals to me. I want to contribute my experience from ten years of Formula E and play a strong role in the World Championship together with Opel and Théo.”

Opel: 'Formula E the perfect stage for high-performance Mokka GSE and Corsa GSE'

Evans made his first official appearance in Opel colours this week as a surprise guest at the international media drive of the new battery-electric Opel Corsa GSE2.

This is just one example of how closely Opel is set to tie its production models with its halo motorsport project; using Formula E as a stage for its all-electric high-performance models.

After the Mokka GSE, which is already on the roads, the Corsa GSE will be launched this year and will make its trade fair debut at the Paris Motor Show in October.

The completion of the driver line-up, which includes Test and Development Driver Sophia Flörsch in addition to Evans and Pourchaire, marks Opel’s next step on the way to the World Championship.

Confirmation of its line up follows the Rüsselsheim-based manufacturer's commitment to the Opel GSE Formula E Team and the world premiere of the Opel GSE 27FE prototype at Le Castellet.

The next major milestone is coming this autumn, when Opel, together with Evans and Pourchaire, will unveil the final design of the race car for the 2026/27 season at the Paris Motor Show on 12 October 2026.

title: Buemi seals 2025/26 ABB Engineered to Outrun Award, while Mortara and Nato end on a high
excerpt:
As the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship reached a dramatic conclusion in London, the finale also heralded two new ABB Engineered to Outrun Award winners – and the overall triumph for a championship legend.

Edoardo Mortara and Norman Nato secured the honours as the biggest risers across the two races in the English capital, marking their first Engineered to Outrun success of the season.

Though the tense title fight naturally stole headlines, Mortara and Nato scoring points from unlikely starting positions on Saturday and Sunday respectively showed the kind of class that runs deep through the field – even if it is out of the immediate spotlight.

Mortara started down in 18th for Saturday’s PIT BOOST race. He ran a longer first stint before his mandatory charging stop, saving a small but critical 2% extra energy compared to the median in the field in the process.

This allowed him to unleash more pace when others diving into the pits gave him clear air, aided by Mortara using six minutes of ATTACK MODE deployment. Though there was a full-course yellow to nullify the last minute and a half of this power advantage, it also facilitated a cheaper pitstop.

That perfect combination meant Mortara leapt from 15th to 8th around the pitstop phase, and the energy advantage he retained after the pitstop allowed him to not only consolidate his position but push on even further.

He was actually fifth at the chequered flag but a final move on Dan Ticktum proved slightly too robust, so a small time penalty relegated him to seventh.

Still, it was a very effective performance – and the manner of his drive turned out to be neatly prescient for what followed a day later, when Mortara completed a Mahindra one-two in qualifying and finished Sunday's race on the podium.

Nato ends on a high

When the season finale exploded into life in the final few laps, claiming various point-scoring casualties in and around the top 10, it presented a clear opportunity for anyone who could keep it clean and be poised to pounce.

Nato was one such driver. Having started towards the back of the field, Nato made little progress from his 19th place grid position for much of the race, as he focused on an extreme energy-saving tactic - building a surplus of more than 5% versus the grid’s median.

By the time he opted to engage ATTACK MODE in the final third of the E-Prix he had moved just one position forward. But that ATTACK MODE timing was absolutely perfect to capitalise on the drama that engulfed the championship battle and massively impacted the lower reaches of the top 10.

Nato gained eight of his nine positions in that phase of the race, and was already on the move in the midfield when a multi-car collision vaulted him to 11th. The last seconds of his ATTACK MODE helped move him into ninth and though team-mate Oliver Rowland's late double ATTACK MODE burst meant the Nissans swapped positions again, this race still ended with Nato snatching a very unlikely point.

Though this has not been a grand season to remember for the championship returnee, he at least ensured it ended on a relative high with just his fourth points finish of the year.

Buemi wins overall

But it was Sebastien Buemi, together with race engineer Connor Summerville, who topped the final leaderboard for the season – pipping Lucas di Grassi and Markus Michelberger by just two places having gained 89 positions over the 17 races this year.

As Buemi leaves Envision Racing after this season, his Formula E future is unknown. The 2015/16 champion has been one of the grid’s most impressive stalwarts with 14 wins, 36 podiums and 1,172 points scored and that experience and class has been at the centre of a strong season.

Buemi has been in the points 11 times out of 17, exemplified by two final flourishes in London where he turned 10th place on the grid in both races to fourth and fifth at the finish.

title: Porsche's GEN3 racer to debut in Need for Speed Mobile
excerpt:
Following its recent launch into one of China's largest mobile games, Game for Peace, the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship has teamed up with Tencent once again.

Starting 21 August, players in China will be able to take the wheel of the title-winning Porsche GEN3 99X Electric, bringing peak electric performance, high-torque acceleration, and energy recovery mechanics to Need for Speed Mobile.

Porsche GEN3 99X Electric in the Hall of Legends

Positioned in the prestigious 'Hall of Legends - Hybrid & Electric Drive' vehicle class, the Porsche GEN3 99X Electric introduces a distinct driving profile specifically calibrated to tackle the high-speed streets of Need for Speed Mobile.

Engineered to replicate the real-world dynamics of Porsche's official Formula E factory contender, the in-game machine boasts several unique handling traits:

Agile Drift Tuning: Features more agile rear-tail behavior during drifts, allowing drivers to carry higher entry speeds through tight corners and execute sharper turn-ins.

High Torque Endurance: Delivers a significantly higher base top speed, precision steering response, and automatic nitrous accumulation while cornering.

ERS Regenerative Braking System: Replicating the 99X Electric’s real-world powertrain management, the Energy Recovery System (ERS) delivers a sustained high-torque launch boost for 2.8 seconds from a standstill. During braking, handbrake turns, and inertia drifts, the system harvests kinetic energy - temporarily lowering top speed - before unleashing the stored power within 2 seconds post-drift for a massive nitrous boost

Exclusive 'Hot Pursuit Mode' capabilities

Beyond standard sprint and circuit battles, driving the Porsche GEN3 99X Electric unlocks dedicated operational perks within Need for Speed Mobile’s high-stakes Hot Pursuit game mode - the classic gameplay format that features intense chases between Street Racers and Pursuit Teams:

Street Racer Role: Equipping the Porsche 99X Electric expands overall backpack capacity, giving racers the room needed to carry extra tactical supplies during intense escapes.

Pursuit Team Role: Drivers taking on the enforcement role will completely eliminate the helicopter cooldown timer while operating the vehicle, maintaining continuous aerial surveillance over targets.

How to unlock: 'Hall Treasures' event

The Porsche GEN3 99X Electric officially debuts on August 21 via the limited-time “Hall Treasures” in-game event. The car can be unlocked using Hall Treasure Coupons to draw from the event pool. Coupons can be acquired through several limited-time mechanics, which can be viewed via the Events menu, within Specials.

Sanjay Shivaram, Brand Licensing & Retail Director at Formula E, said: "China is a key market for Formula E, and teaming up with Porsche to bring the Porsche GEN3 99X Electric to Need for Speed Mobile allows us to connect millions of gamers with the speed of electric performance, and this iconic automotive brand.

"Tencent has brilliantly translated our real-world tech - such as kinetic energy recovery - into the game, and Need for Speed is one of the most famous racing franchises in the world, so we’re thrilled to be able to contribute to its journey.”

title: Reaction from a title-deciding Formula E weekend
excerpt:
The paddock reacts to a title-deciding weekend in the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship.

Pascal Wehrlein

"Under the circumstances we had today, very special. Even though I must say the first one is always a bit more exciting. That's definitely the case, but today it was definitely a tough race. Never expected that what happened would happen, but, anyways, it is what it is. We made it.

"We set the base for today, in the last 15-16 races and we took over the lead yesterday again. The approach of the whole weekend was phenomenal, what a job we've done so far. A bit of an up-and-down season, but again, in the end, you know, when there's pressure on, when it matters, when it counts, we're pretty good.

"Obviously it was a bit unpredictable what Antonio did and how far he took it, but, you know, credits to him for what he did in this race. I think under normal circumstances during that race, we would have had a nice race, probably another podium finish, but nevertheless, I think we achieved what we had to achieve, and we did what we had to do."

Jake Dennis

"There was a clear chance. I think everything we did today, we executed perfectly. We put ourselves in a position to take the title. We were ahead at points, until we weren't. So, yeah, I think we did everything right today.

"I mean, he (Pascal) took me cleanly straight out of the race, so it's as simple as that. I think from my side, it's quite obvious. I think it's embarrassing in what we've seen today from Pascal, Porsche, to be in that position to be Pascal clearly ahead, and then he just rams me straight into the wall. It's quite surprising, but ultimately if they want to win it like that, then they can. But that's the game.

"I can leave London with my head held high. I'm happy with the way I drove, the risks I took, and yeah, I go into the off-season in a pretty good headspace. I have a lot of things personally going on in my life with my fiancée, you know, giving birth in a few weeks, so it's going to be a cool period. GEN4 is going to be exciting, and obviously I'm super busy with BMW still, so from my side an exciting few months coming up, so very much looking forward to it."

Mitch Evans

"I think ultimately we just, unfortunately, both days qualified behind the wrong car. Either a blue and white roadblock for the last two days, and they did all they could to stop me. You know, I managed to get past them in today's race, but ultimately just lost too much ground to the front guys, and yeah, it was for me a little bit extreme, but it is what it is. We did what we had to do on our side to try and give ourselves a shot, and I think we did that. But ultimately we just lost it in quali both days, but we tried and we didn't give up.

"I obviously wanted a different ending to my journey at the team, but wasn't meant to be. I don't leave with many regrets, to be fair. I knew this day was going to come at some point, especially with a lot on the line, and this team's given me so much, and I'm forever grateful for that. They've given me my first professional contract in the sport, and I owe so much to them and everyone that's been involved in the project since day one.

"I'm very proud of what we've achieved, obviously wanted more, we had one last box to check, and we unfortunately haven't done that, but a lot to be proud of. It's going to be weird waking up tomorrow not as a Jaguar driver for the first time. But I just wish them the best for the future."

Ian James (Jaguar TCS Racing)

"I'll be briefly honest, coming into this weekend, I knew how much was at stake in both championships, how much not only Mitch, but we as a team, wanted to deliver the Drivers' Championship for him and for the team as well. And there was always that risk, I suppose, that we'd let our emotions get the better of us. But all credit to the guy on my right (Evans) and to the whole team as well, because the emotions were very much kept in check.

"We approached every session with a clear and level head and executed as well as we possibly could. As Mitch said, qualifying didn't go our way, and that played a huge role then in the outcomes of both races. But at the end of the day, I'm hugely proud of both Mitch and Antonio and the whole team. It's a phenomenal way to deliver a Teams' World Championship."

Thomas Laudenbach (Porsche)

"I have to say that for us, it's great to win again the Manufacturer title. I mean, we are a car manufacturer, but we're also running a team, and but I guess it's the right time to say that this is an effort not only of our team, this is an effort of also the Andretti Formula E team, of CUPRA KIRO, and all together we scored points and secured the title. So for us, that's very important, and we're proud of that. And if you ask me how we celebrate, it's going to be a good one, I can tell you!

"This year the fight with Jaguar, I think that's what the spectators want to see, what the fans want to see. Sometimes the luck is on your side, sometimes you have bad luck. But I mean, that's sport. For today, we are, I think we can all be happy that we provided a good race today for the spectators, and extremely proud of the achievement this season."

title: History in the making: Taylor Barnard becomes Formula E’s youngest winner
excerpt:
On the day that Formula E crowned a new champion, DS PENSKE's Taylor Barnard made some history of his own.

Youngest driver to start a Formula E race, youngest pole sitter and youngest driver to claim a podium. Heading into the final race weekend of the 2025/26 season, DS PENSKE's Taylor Barnard was missing just one record (and arguably the most important one) - to be named Formula E's youngest race winner.

REPORT: Wehrlein navigates dramatic finale to seal Drivers' title as Barnard wins in London

Barnard joined the French squad at the start of the season, following NEOM McLaren's exit from the championship, and despite showing moments of promise and raw pace over the course of the 2025/26 campaign, he has struggled to replicate the impressive points scoring haul of his rookie year.

But heading into the final day of the season, with most eyes on the fight at the head of the championship, British-born Barnard quietly put together a confident and assured performance in qualifying, placing him 6th on the grid for the E-Prix. In the race, Barnard remained in contention throughout, closely following the Mahindra Racing duo of Nyck de Vries and Edoardo Mortara.

The winning moment came in the closing stages of the race, when Barnard's late ATTACK MODE activation saw him able to muscle by Mortara for P2, then polesitter de Vries for the win with a sneaky dive up the inside of the Season 8 champion into the final turn with just two laps left to run.

"I think playing around the championship games was obviously important," said Formula E's newest race winner. "As soon as I got to P3 and I had Antonio behind me, I knew there was going to be some games going on, so it almost felt like a podium secured at that point. And then I was just trying to do everything I can to get as much advantage on the Mahindras as possible.

I didn't think it was going to be possible, they both had two minutes more energy. So, yeah, to be able to get both of them, honestly, is unreal."

At 22 years and 76 days old, Barnard becomes the youngest race winner in Formula E history, taking the record from his DS PENSKE teammate Maximilian Gunther, who won the 2020 Santiago E-Prix at 22 years and 200 days old. And after a long season of highs and lows, surely the result gives the young Brit a big dose of confidence heading into the off season.

"I've now got two complete seasons in Formula E under my belt," he says. "And it's been a long learning process, but obviously the longer I'm going, the more experience I'm getting and the better I'm getting generally at the races, so it's going to keep going. But obviously, it's a massive confidence boost for the team as well. It's been such a tough season, so everybody deserves it."

Taylor Barnard finishes the 2025/26 season 11th in the Drivers' Championship on 68 points.
